raw_response:
I farm only 5.2 mu, and I am 75, so I will keep things simple, stable, and familiar. I have spent many years on a wheat-maize rotation in north China, and with well irrigation I will stay with that system on all of my land because it matches my experience and spreads income across the year. I do not want risky changes. For wheat, I will use an improved variety rather than old seed because I want steady emergence, good tillering, and reliable grain filling. I will plough or rotary-work the land after maize depending on residue, then keep fertilizer moderate but sufficient, with more nitrogen than phosphorus and potassium, because wheat on irrigated land responds well but too much input is wasteful on such a small farm. I will irrigate about three times for wheat: around overwintering, jointing, and grain filling if needed. For maize, I will follow immediately after wheat harvest on the same 5.2 mu. I will use hybrid seed because maize benefits clearly from it, and I want stronger yield on limited land. Since labor matters at my age, I will use no-tillage or very light tillage after wheat harvest to save time and moisture. I will give maize enough nitrogen and some phosphorus and potassium, irrigate about twice if rainfall is not enough, and spray only as needed for the common weeds and insects. My goal is not maximum yield at any cost; I will manage for dependable production, manageable labor, and low risk.
